text:
nina_engineer: quick Q — I just started contributing after-tax (non-Roth) to the 401k bucket because I hit the Roth limit. I heard we can do in-plan Roth conversions for after-tax money. Is that allowed with our plan? Also curious how a plan loan gets handled if I later terminate — does a loan offset impact my ability to convert?

omar_benefits: hey @nina_engineer :wave: short answers: 1) our plan allows in-plan Roth conversions of after-tax contributions, but only if the vendor/process supports it and plan admin has enabled the feature. 2) loan offsets happen when a termination occurs and the outstanding loan is treated as a distribution if not repaid — that reduces your rollover-eligible balance, which can affect conversions.

nina_engineer: thx. timeline / paperwork wise, what do I need to do to request a conversion? can I schedule it quarterly or is it continuous?

omar_benefits: good Q. Forus (our trustee) supports both ad-hoc conversions and periodic batch processing. We usually run conversions monthly on the 15th so they hit with minimal tax-year timing issues. You'll need to complete the Forus "In-Plan Roth Conversion" form and confirm the source sub-account. I'll attach sample fields below.

omar_benefits: Sample form snippet:
```
Participant: Nina E.
Account#: 12345678
Source: After-Tax Employee Contributions
Target: Roth 401(k) Subaccount
Amount: $XXXX or "ALL"
Requested Conversion Date: 2026-06-15
```

kate_payroll: adding payroll/legal nuance — conversions are taxable events for the year they're processed (taxable earnings on earnings portion). after-tax basis moves tax-free, but any earnings on after-tax deferrals are taxable when converted. recommend consulting a tax advisor. Also: loan offsets reduce the balance that can be rolled to an IRA; if you offset a loan at termination, that offset amount is reported as taxable distribution.

forus-rep: Forus here — confirming we accept in-plan Roth conversions for Redwood participants. We need signed authorization + 5 business days to process if ad-hoc. For terminated participants, standard flow: if loan unpaid at separation, plan admin may treat it as offset; offseted amount is reported on Form 1099-R. We also offer a rollover window for eligible amounts.

nina_engineer: got it. If I convert now and then later leave the company with an outstanding loan, will the conversion complicate rollover to an IRA?

omar_benefits: conversion funds that are already Roth within the plan can be rolled to a Roth IRA later (subject to Roth rollover rules). But any loan offset would reduce pre-tax/after-tax balances available to roll. Conversion itself doesn't stop you from rolling converted Roth amounts, but watch tax timing and 5-year rules for qualified distributions.

benefits-bot: Helpful links: https://benefits.redwood.example/in-plan-roth-conversions and https://benefits.redwood.example/loans-and-termination (see "Loan Offsets")

kate_payroll: action items for @nina_engineer: 1) confirm amount you want to convert and requested date; 2) sign the Forus conversion form (we can e-sign); 3) if you have an outstanding loan and think you might leave soon, DM payroll so we can discuss repayment vs. offset strategy.

nina_engineer: thanks y'all. I'll DM Omar the amount and ask Forus to schedule on 2026-06-15. Also will DM Kate about repayment timing. :thumbsup:
